subject: religious-studies
intro: Religious studies leads to paid work at the centre of faith communities — leading worship and teaching, directing religious education programmes, and supporting people through the life stages the course studies.

roles.title: Clergy
roles.what: Conduct religious worship and perform the spiritual functions associated with their faith's beliefs and practices, providing spiritual and moral guidance and assistance to members of the congregation.
roles.where: The syllabus's worship unit — communal and private worship, the roles of leaders in the church and mosque — and the beliefs-and-scriptures unit are the working knowledge clergy draw on to lead services and counsel members.

roles.title: Directors, Religious Activities and Education
roles.what: Coordinate or design programmes and conduct outreach that promotes the religious education and activities of a denominational group, and provide counselling and guidance on family and personal matters.
roles.where: The festivals-and-fasts and rites-of-passage units supply the yearly and lifelong programmes these directors schedule, while pilgrimage units such as Hajj inform the events and teaching materials they plan.

roles.title: Philosophy and Religion Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach philosophy, religion and theology courses at colleges and universities — lecturing on belief systems, sacred texts and ethics, and usually researching and writing in their specialism.
roles.where: The syllabus's comparative structure — Christian beliefs about God and the Bible alongside the Six Articles of Faith and Usul ad-Din — is the multi-faith literacy these teachers expect students to bring.

roles.title: Social and Human Service Assistants
roles.what: Assist social workers, psychologists and other providers in delivering client services across fields such as rehabilitation and family support — helping people find benefits and community services.
roles.where: The rites-of-passage-and-family-life unit — how communities mark birth, marriage and death — builds the cultural and pastoral sensitivity assistants need when supporting families through hard times.
